source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 17 January 1923, p. 5 ("The municipal elections: the results"); Irish News, 17 January 1923, p. 5 ("Catholic party in Corporation"); Northern Whig, 17 January 1923, p. 5
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: figures read from the page images of the News-Letter's ward results (INA block images) and checked against the Irish News; names and full forms from the News-Letter's list of nominations; unopposed members are the only remaining nominees for the seats after the withdrawals reported on 8 January

note: Election of the whole of Belfast Corporation (an alderman and three councillors in each of the 15 wards) by direct vote, proportional representation having been abolished; nominations 5 January, poll Monday 15 January 1923, counted 16 January. Eight aldermen and nine councillors (St Anne's, Pottinger and Windsor) were returned unopposed at nomination, and withdrawals left the Duncairn and Victoria councillors unopposed (Belfast News-Letter, 6 and 8 January 1923). State of parties in the new Corporation: Official Unionists 43, Independent Unionists 7, Nationalists 3, Labour 2 (News-Letter, 17 January 1923). E.W. = Expelled Workers' nominees (News-Letter, 6 January 1923). 413 spoiled papers in the councillors' poll.
correctionNote: Corrected from the Belfast Corporation register of members (PRONI LA/7/1/CA/1/3): D. M'Randall's vote is 3,202 as the register records it (previously 3,302, from the newspaper source). Checked on the page image of the Belfast News-Letter, 17 January 1923, p. 5 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the three elected members' surnames, printed in capitals, are entered in the round's normal case (Hopkins, M'Keown, M'Alevey); the paper prints M'Randall 3,302 against the register's 3,202 and prints no majority or poll to decide, so the register figure is kept. Checked on the page image of the Irish News, 17 January 1923, p. 5 (w8-review, Nov 2026): the Irish News also prints M'Randal 3,302 and no councillorship majority or poll, so two papers print 3,302 against the register's 3,202; the register's figure is kept under the register rule (no printed arithmetic decides) pending a re-check of the register entry. Set to 3,302 (research-J W8R-1, owner-approved 13 Nov 2026): a third paper, the Northern Whig of 17 January 1923, p. 5, prints M'Randall, D. (I.) 3,302 (it prints Mercier 3,343 where the News-Letter misprinted 3,434, so it was set independently); the News-Letter, the Irish News and the Whig all print 3,302. The register of members (PRONI LA/7/1/CA/1/3) as read gives 3,202; its transcription misreads 2 for 3 elsewhere.
